openFindings.title: The history-engine CI step cannot resolve tsc on a clean runner
The history-engine CI step cannot resolve `tsc` on a clean runner
openFindings.description: The `build` script hardcodes `../../../skills/system-spec-kit/node_modules/.bin/tsc`, which resolves to `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/node_modules/.bin/tsc`. The workflow's engine step (`spec-kit-check.yml:301`) runs `npm --prefix .skilled/hooks/session-handover/history run build`, but the workflow installs only `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit` (`:227`) and `.skilled` (`:230`). `.skilled/package.json` declares no `workspaces` field, so `npm ci` at `.skilled` provisions `.skilled/node_modules` only and never creates the `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/node_modules` tree the build script names. The registry anchor (`line: 6`) points at the `engines` field; the proving anchor is `:11`.

openFindings.title: Engine-only changes never run the engine vitest suites
openFindings.description: Both trigger filters (`push` `:6-44`, `pull_request` `:47-85`) list `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/**` but not `.skilled/hooks/**`, so a change confined to `.skilled/hooks/session-handover/history/**` does not trigger the workflow whose `runtime-vitest` job runs the engine build and suite (`:296-302`).

openFindings.title: The pinned 66-character bound is only behaviourally pinned in one direction
openFindings.description: The hook-state copy (`:278,281-284`) and the engine copy (`lookup-offer.ts:33,52-58`) remain equal at 66 with the same quote transform, so the residual is the pinning asymmetry: the engine tests hold the copies equal behaviourally, not by comparing the constants, so a hook-state-side edit can drift without an engine-side failure.

openFindings.title: The lookup offer interpolates the runtime label into a model-pasted shell command
openFindings.description: `SPECKIT_RUNTIME=${locator.runtime} ` is inserted raw into the command text at `:70`; the schema enum is the only guard, and this module does not re-validate. No in-tree producer passes an unsafe label, so impact stays P2.
